title: Introduce micro-window aggregation + delayed-batch sampling to minimize tracing hotpath overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Tracing instrumentation at the ingress and router hotpaths is adding measurable CPU and allocation overhead at high QPS. Existing tail-based and probabilistic schemes reduce volume but still cause ~15-30% p95 latency regressions during bursts because span encoding and metadata allocation happen synchronously on the request path. Goal: reduce hotpath cost to <5% p95 regression at 99th percentile load while preserving enough fidelity for tail analysis and debugging.

Proposal summary: implement a micro-window aggregation + delayed-batch commit mechanism that:
- coalesces low-value spans into compact, low-fidelity summaries in the hotpath ("micro-aggregates") using a fixed-size ring buffer per worker instead of allocating full span objects;
- defers heavy work (json/protobuf encoding, attribute enrichment, sampling decision commit) to a background batcher that wakes on micro-window flush triggers (time budget or token budget thresholds);
- implements a lightweight outlier bypass: spans that exceed a latency/error heuristic are marked with a 1-bit flag and immediately enqueued to a small high-priority queue to ensure tail-capture accuracy;
- uses a fidelity-tiered reservoir for sampled spans: majority of commits are low-fidelity sketches (small maps of attributes + trace id), a small reservoir holds full-span payloads for recent outliers and errors;
- keeps sampling policy adaptive based on per-route latency histograms and recent SLO violations, so noisy routes get higher retention without increasing global hotpath cost.

Trade-offs considered:
- fidelity vs cost: low-fidelity aggregates lose attribute-level details for many spans; mitigated by reserving full-span slots for outliers and on-demand rehydration hooks (can fetch raw KV cache on-demand for a trace id).
- eventual consistency: delayed commits mean some spans appear later in dashboards (seconds-level), acceptable for investigative workflows but not for real-time alerting; alerts remain wired to lightweight error counters on the hotpath.
- complexity: adds background workers and new buffers; accepted because it centralizes encoding/IO and reduces CPU pressure across many services.

Success criteria (measurable):
- hotpath CPU usage down by >=25% on high QPS benchmarks (8k RPS simulated ingress),
- end-to-end tracing costs (bytes and requests to trace store) reduced >=40%,
- ability to reconstruct tail traces for 95% of SLO breaches within 60s,
- no increase in customer-visible error rates or request latencies beyond 5% p95.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrument micro-aggregate ring buffer and low-cost flagging primitives (hotpath, no allocations): branch prototype in platform repo.
2) Background batcher service with token-budget flush and priority queue for outliers; implement backpressure when trace store is slow.
3) Sampling policy controller that consumes latency histograms and adjusts reservoir/commit thresholds per-route.
4) End-to-end tests + perf harness against staging trace store and a shadow traffic run.
5) Canary rollout with feature flag per-cluster, monitor dashboards and rollback path.

Telemetry and observability for rollout:
- new dashboards: "micro-agg:hotpath-savings", "sampling-reservoir-util", "trace-commit-latency" (links in comments)
- automated alert: reservoir-fill > 80% for > 5m or trace-commit-latency median > 2s

Docs & artifacts:
- design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Micro-Window+Aggregation+Design
- perf harness and scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/main/tools/trace-perf-harness
- implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3489
- dashboard: https://console.redwood.io/dashboards/trace-sampling-microagg

2026-01-25 Dev Review - Kenji Rao: Reviewed background batcher API. Concern: need robust backpressure to avoid unbounded mem growth if trace store backends are slow. Action: add per-tenant token bucket and throttle signal to router.

2026-01-28 Diego Alvarez: Implemented token-bucket backpressure and high-priority bypass queue for flagged outliers. Local perf now shows 27% CPU drop, p95 request latency regressions reduced from 18% -> 4% under synthetic burst.
2026-01-30 PM Review - Aisha Patel: Verified feature meets product goals. Requested telemetry for 'percent tail-reconstructable' metric. Added to success criteria and test harness.

2026-02-02 Diego Alvarez: PR #3489 updated with guard and improved metrics. Next: schedule a 10% traffic canary next week and collect 72h of telemetry before ramp.
